core_obligations: Apply the topological criterion (proof lines 18176-18181): the underlying space of X is spectral, so it remains to show, for every irreducible closed subscheme Y of X, that Y cap Z = Y x_{Spec(A)} Spec(A/I) is connected.

Reduce to the irreducible case and Stein factorisation (proof lines 18182-18190): replacing X by Y one may assume X irreducible and must show Z connected; taking the Stein factorisation X -> Spec(B) -> Spec(A) of f makes A -> B integral and (B, IB) a henselian pair, so one may assume the fibres of X -> Spec(A) are geometrically connected.

Use properness and the henselian connectedness input (proof lines 18191-18193): the image T of f is irreducible and closed since X is proper over A, so T cap V(I) is connected by the henselian-pair connectedness lemma.

Conclude (proof lines 18194-18197): the map Y x_{Spec(A)} Spec(A/I) -> T cap V(I) is a surjective closed map with connected fibres, so the quotient criterion for connected components applies and gives connectedness of Y cap Z, which is what the criterion required.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the connectedness of Y cap Z for irreducible Y using the topological h^0 criterion and spectrality.
Replace X by its Stein factorisation to assume geometrically connected fibres over the henselian base.
Use properness to make the closed image irreducible and apply the connectedness lemma for henselian pairs, then the connected-fibres criterion.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the Zariski-topological companion of Gabber's comparison: sections of a sheaf on a proper scheme over a henselian pair agree with sections on the closed fibre (statement lines 18167-18173). The proof (proof lines 18175-18197) applies the topological h^0 criterion, reduces by Stein factorisation to geometrically connected fibres over a henselian pair, uses properness to control the closed image and the connectedness lemma for henselian pairs, and finishes with the connected-fibres criterion for quotient maps. H2: one reduction plus one connectedness argument, written out.
